Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: You just read the script, learn your lines and perform them — the playwright has already written everything you need. Correct: A script is a blueprint, not a building. Describe how you would interpret a scene from a play you have studied for performance. Explain your director's concept and how it would shape your staging choices.

Script interpretation tests AO1 (knowledge of dramatic terms), AO2 (analysing how meaning is created), and AO3 (performance choices). The written exam (Component 1, Section A) asks about a set text — you must show how a performer, designer or director would realise the text. Always match your answer to the perspective specified in the question.

Interpreting a script for performance begins with rigorous text analysis that uncovers the dramatic possibilities within the writing. The first read-through focuses on the overall story: what happens, to whom, and why.
